title: Entertain, then Cancel: How Thinking Makes Reasoning Models Read Some and Or Literally
abstract: arXiv:2610.21204v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When a speaker says ``some students passed'', listeners infer that not all of them did. Reasoning models now let users decide how long a model thinks before it answers, but we do not know what extra thinking does to such everyday inferences. We study this directly: we keep a model's weights fixed, change only how much it thinks, and record which reading it chooses. A second tool cuts the model's own reasoning at successive points and asks for an answer, showing where the reading changes. Thinking makes models read logical words as logic: it cancels the implicatures of \emph{some} (\emph{not all}) and \emph{or} (\emph{not both}) in most tested open reasoning models and in GPT-5, while context-driven inferences such as indirect answers improve. The trace shows why: models first entertain the enriched reading and cancel it later. Answering from that early reading, an exploratory inference-time remedy, recovers these implicatures without los

translated_title: 先设想，后取消：思考如何使推理模型按字面理解 "some" 与 "or"
translated_abstract: 当说话者说“一些学生通过了”时，听者会推断并非所有学生都通过了。如今的推理模型允许用户决定模型在回答前思考多长时间，但我们尚不清楚额外的思考会给这类日常推理带来什么影响。我们直接研究了这一问题：保持模型权重不变，只改变其思考量，并记录模型选择的解读方式；另一个工具则在连续的多个时间点截断模型自身的推理并要求其给出答案，以揭示解读在何处发生转变。研究显示，思考使模型将逻辑词当作纯粹的逻辑来解读：在多数被测的开源推理模型以及 GPT-5 中，"some"（并非所有）与"or"（并非两者）的会话含义被取消，而诸如间接回答等依赖语境的推理反而有所改善。推理轨迹揭示了原因：模型会先设想这种丰富化的解读，随后再将其取消。在早期解读阶段就作答——一种探索性的推理时补救方法——能够在不……（摘要在此处截断）的情况下恢复这些含义。
tldr: 增加思考会使推理模型把"some"和"or"按字面逻辑理解——先设想、后取消其日常会话含义（如"some"意味着“并非所有”），而在早期解读阶段作答可恢复这些含义。
en_tdlr: Longer thinking makes reasoning models read "some" and "or" literally—first entertaining and then cancelling their everyday implicatures—and answering from the early enriched reading restores them.
